<!--
Shared OJS preamble for charted articles. Include it once, near the top of the
body, with an include shortcode naming this file relative to the article:
`../_theme/_ojs-setup.qmd`. The shortcode is not spelled out here because
Quarto resolves includes in a pre-engine text pass that does not respect HTML
comments -- a literal one on this line would include this file into itself and
recurse until the stack blows.

It defines three reactive values every Observable Plot figure on this site
needs: `contentWidth`, `figW`, and `col`. Deliberately no frontmatter -- an
included file contributes body content only, and its own metadata would be
ignored. The leading underscore keeps Quarto from rendering it as a page.
-->

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
// Quarto's builtin `width` measures the Quarto frame, which is wider than the
// column the text actually occupies, so a figure sized from it overflows and
// gets a scrollbar. Measure the content element instead; Generators.observe
// also makes this reactive to a window resize.
//
// main#quarto-document-content is the reading column. Falling straight through
// to document.body would silently measure the viewport, so the fallback is a
// last resort rather than a normal path.
contentWidth = Generators.observe((notify) => {
  const el = document.querySelector("main#quarto-document-content") ?? document.body
  const read = () => notify(el.getBoundingClientRect().width)
  read()
  const observer = new ResizeObserver(read)
  observer.observe(el)
  return () => observer.disconnect()
})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
figW = Math.max(300, Math.min(contentWidth, 720))
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
// Plot writes its marks as SVG attributes, which take a literal colour rather
// than a var(...) reference, so the palette is read off the page once. The
// chart tokens are shared by both themes, so there is nothing to re-read when
// the theme toggle fires.
//
// Read from body, not documentElement: the preview bundles define --qmd-* on a
// plain :root, but custom properties inherit, so body resolves under either
// selector. No fallback colour -- the tokens are generated from tokens.yaml and
// always present, and a silent fallback would hide the one failure worth
// seeing.
col = {
  const cs = getComputedStyle(document.body)
  const v = (k) => cs.getPropertyValue(k).trim()
  return {
    ink: v("--qmd-chart-ink"),
    series: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6].map((i) => v(`--qmd-chart-series-${i}`)),
  }
}
```
